title: Umberling dataops — call capture and fast follow
body:
Call: Umberling DataOps kickoff (15m) — quick capture Date: 2026-02-10 10:00 PT Attendees: Sarah Cheng (Umberling eng), Leo Ortiz (DataOps), Priya Rao (Security), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Devon Park (Redwood Solutions) Objective: understand immediate onramp constraints, minimum MVP for private deployment, SLOs and tortoise/hare risk factors. TL;DR - Customer wants Private (VPC) deployment behind their TGW for PII workloads; legal/infosec requires KMS + HSM integration and audit logs retained 12 months. - Latency target: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms for short chat requests (<= 256 tokens). Prefer batching disabled for chat-first flows; allow batched embedding jobs. - Model: prefer open LLM (Llama3-type-ish) 30–40B FP16/4bit quantized. They want fallback to smaller 7B quantized for emergencies. Notes / raw capture (shorthand) - Network: Umberling uses 2 AZs in us-west-2, strict egress rules. They can open specific IP ranges or use Transit Gateway peering. Ask networking about IP allowlist vs. AWS PrivateLink. - Security: Priya insisted on customer-managed KMS for keys used by Redwood Private. Also HSM-backed signing for audit records (optional). Need to confirm KMS key policy + cross-account IAM roles. - Data residency: workloads and logs must stay in us-west-2. No log replication to other regions. Retention 12 months, searchable (ELK or CloudWatch). - Storage: embedding store will be their RDS + S3; they prefer S3 for snapshot KV caches. Need a small adapter to push Redwood cache snapshots to their S3 prefix. - Throughput: initial traffic ~20 qps (chat reqs), burst to 200 qps over three months. Will likely commit to Dedicated or Private capacity after POC. - Tokens: average request ~120 tokens in/out. Long-form generation not in scope for phase 1. - Auth: they will use JWT issued by Okta; we must validate issuer and integrate with their IdP for console access. Service-to-service between their infra and Redwood control-plane will use short-lived certs. Gotchas / potential blockers - Tokenization mismatch: their prompt templates use non-ASCII glyphs and embedded HTML; need to validate tokenizer equivalence between their preprocessor and the model runtime (we had a similar issue with glyphs -> tokens exploding). - Legacy event pipeline emits chat turns with incremental context via JSON attachments (not plain text). We need a lightweight transform layer or adapter to flatten into prompt. - Disk space for KV cache snapshots: they want to persist per-customer cache for fast warm starts; sizing estimate needed (RW inference ops will help). - Admin UX: they requested a simple toggle in the console to fallback to the 7B variant during capacity pressure. We can support via rollout policy but UX will need a one-click control for them. Config/ops hints (notes-to-self) - Recommend initial Private deployment with 2 worker pools: pool-A (40B quantized, target p50 80–120ms), pool-B (7B fallback). Use smart routing: prefer pool-A, fallback to pool-B on either GPU pressure or emergent errors. - Autoscaling: set cooldowns aggressively for chat SLOs; prefer vertical scale (smaller GPU counts, but higher instance count) to keep token latency stable. - Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for system prompts and common first-turn prompt templates; their UX has a lot of identical system messages across sessions — big win. Action items / next steps - Sofia: send follow-up note with list of required IAM roles + key policy template (due 2026-02-11). - Devon: prototype S3-based cache snapshot adapter and share design doc (due 2026-02-18). Link to draft: GitHub PR above. - Umberling (Sarah): provide sample event payloads (3 examples) showing JSON attachment format and one with HTML entities (due 2026-02-13). - Rina: spin up a quick tokenizer test harness to compare token counts for sample prompts on 40B model vs their preprocessor (due 2026-02-16). - Operations: schedule a short infra scoping call w/ network/security (30m) — propose 2026-02-17. Open questions we must resolve before POC - Does Umberling accept Redwood-managed egress IP ranges or require Transit Gateway/PrivateLink? (affects timeline) - Will they allow us to store anonymized usage metrics for debugging? If not, we need an alternative observability plan (more verbose local logs + periodic snapshots). - HSM signing: mandatory or optional? If mandatory this adds procurement and timeline complexity. Notes to self (messy) - Ask infra if A100S vs L40 is cheaper for quantized 40B in our bench. L40 might be better single-token perf for 4bit. - Consider offering a short-term dedicated pool on Hosted to get initial SLA while Private infra is being provisioned (sales may like shorter runway). - Prepare a one-pager for legal explaining how audit logs are exported and who can access them (map to their compliance reqs). Appendix: example prompt transform (pseudo) -- original payload (from Sarah): { "user_id": "u-12345", "turns": [ {"role":"user","text":"
Hello — my acct # is <EM>ABC123</EM>"}, {"role":"assistant","text":"..."} ], "attachments": [{"type":"snippet","content":"

Order #9876

"}] } -- transform notes: strip HTML tags, preserve emphasis token markers, normalize unicode, dedupe repeated system messages, collapse attachments into appended plaintext block. End of capture. Will refine after tokenizer tests + sample payloads arrive. Sofia M.
